preguntas.pregunta: On what date was the Apollo 11 mission launched from the Kennedy Space Center?

opciones.texto: April 12, 1969, the date of the first crewed U.S. orbital flight.
July 16, 1969, the date the Saturn V was launched from the Kennedy Center.
July 20, 1969, the day the spacecraft entered lunar orbit.
July 4, 1969, the date of the historic Apollo 11 Moon landing.

preguntas.explicacion: The launch took place on July 16, 1969, when the Saturn V lifted off from the Kennedy Center.

preguntas.pregunta: Which astronaut stayed in the Columbia Command Module while the others descended in the lunar module?

opciones.texto: Buzz Aldrin, pilot of the Eagle lunar module.
James Lovell, pilot of the Gemini command module.
Neil Armstrong, commander of the Eagle lunar module.
Michael Collins, pilot of the Columbia command module.

preguntas.explicacion: Michael Collins stayed in the Columbia command module to watch over the ship and prepare for the return.

preguntas.pregunta: What error code did the navigation computer show during the descent to the Mare Tranquillitatis?

opciones.texto: Code 1101, indicating a minor sensor failure.
Code 1405, related to a fuel problem.
Code 1202, signaling a saturation of the navigation processor.
Code 1300, referring to a loss of communication.

preguntas.explicacion: The number 1202 appeared when the navigation processor became overloaded, forcing manual intervention.

preguntas.pregunta: Why was it necessary for Neil Armstrong to take manual control during the Moon landing?

opciones.texto: Because NASA wanted to demonstrate the astronauts' ability to fly without automatic assistance.
Because the radio signal with Earth had been interrupted, preventing any automatic command.
Because error 1202 caused the computer to stop tracking the trajectory, forcing Armstrong to fly manually to avoid craters and save fuel.
Because the lunar module had lost all electrical power, requiring manual control to maintain the orbit.

preguntas.explicacion: The computer failure forced Armstrong to fly manually to ensure a safe and efficient landing.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the use of the space sextant illustrate the challenges of navigation without terrestrial references?

opciones.texto: The sextant allowed the astronauts to fix their position using stars, which demanded precise calculations and compensation for the spacecraft's motion.
The sextant was mainly a training tool for the pilots, with no practical use in the mission.
The sextant served as a backup to the GPS system, which was not available at the time.
The sextant was used to measure the distance to Earth, helping to calibrate the temperature sensors.

preguntas.explicacion: Without GPS, the astronauts relied on the sextant to orient themselves using the stars, which required meticulous calculations.

preguntas.pregunta: What was the main scientific objective of the instruments installed on the lunar surface?

opciones.texto: The passive seismometers and laser retroreflectors were installed to record lunar tremors and measure the Earth-Moon distance, data essential for geology and navigation.
The solar panels were installed to test power generation on the lunar surface.
The photography instruments were brought to capture panoramic images of the lunar landscape.
The American flag and the communication module were placed to demonstrate human presence and maintain contact with Earth.

preguntas.explicacion: The seismometers and retroreflectors provided data on lunar seismic activity and the Earth-Moon distance.

preguntas.pregunta: If the lunar module had run out of fuel during the descent, which phase of the mission would have been most affected and why?

opciones.texto: The Moon landing would have failed, since without enough fuel the module could not have controlled its descent or avoided dangerous terrain.
Reentry would have been impossible, since the module needed fuel to deploy the parachutes.
The docking in lunar orbit would have been unfeasible, since the command module required fuel for the rendezvous maneuver.
The initial launch would have been canceled, since the Saturn V rocket needed fuel to reach Earth orbit.

preguntas.explicacion: Without enough fuel the module could not have completed the controlled descent needed to land on the Moon.

preguntas.pregunta: What biological concern was addressed by the quarantine protocols after the splashdown?

opciones.texto: Reduce the astronauts' exposure to cosmic radiation during the transfer to the quarantine center.
Protect the scientific instruments from contamination by human bacteria when handling lunar samples.
Prevent the possible transmission of extraterrestrial microorganisms to the terrestrial biosphere, ensuring biological safety.
Prevent the leak of classified information about the ship's technology to the public.

preguntas.explicacion: The quarantine protocols were designed to prevent possible extraterrestrial pathogens from contaminating Earth.
